MODX Orchestra

Sixteen Parts of a MODX Performance for reading full scores: one per section of the orchestra, with voices to try for each and a button to hear each one on the board.

Set up for later: a second Performance on the MODX for the full scores, one Part per section of the orchestra, so a score can play on the board’s orchestral voices instead of the site’s samples. The full-score player does not send to the MODX yet; this page is the plan for its sixteen Parts and lets you try each voice on the board now.

Make the Performance

  1. Start from an empty Performance (or any one, then replace its Parts) and give each Part below its voice: touch the Part, then [CATEGORY SEARCH] and the category shown (Strings, Woodwind, Brass, Chromatic Perc, Drum/Perc) to find the name.
  2. Part n plays on channel n: with Utility → Settings → MIDI → MIDI I/O Mode = Multi, each channel reaches only its Part.
  3. Arpeggios and motion sequences off on every Part; Keyboard Control off on all but the one you want to play from the keys.
  4. A hall reverb for the whole Performance; each Part’s reverb send a little higher for the strings than for the brass.
  5. Store it as a User Performance named Site Orchestra, separate from the Site Band one.

The names below come from Yamaha’s MODX+ Data List, read through its PDF text, where the table’s columns run together: check the spelling on the board. Bold is the first to try. Write what you choose in the last column; it is kept in this browser.

Connect

Not connected

▶ plays a short broken chord in the middle of that instrument's range on its channel (a few hits on the percussion Part), so you can hear the voice you loaded. Load the Site Orchestra Performance first.

The sixteen Parts

Staff names: which full-score staves go to the Part (the full-score player names its instruments in Italian, English or German). A score with more staves than this (two flutes and a piccolo, four horns) shares a Part within the family; the "also" line says which voice to use if a doubling instrument has its own staff.

Still to do

  • The full-score player sends each staff to its Part (as the band does through modx.js), with a Site / MODX switch.
  • Pizzicato, tremolo and mutes: a score marks them and the player does not play them yet. On the MODX they need another voice (Pizzicato Strings, Tremolo Strings) or a Scene on the string Parts; no Parts are left in sixteen, so a Scene switch is the likely way.
  • Dynamics: the player shapes velocity from the written dynamics (“Even out the loudness”); the MODX string and brass voices change colour with velocity, so they may need the velocity range set per Part, as the band’s instruments have on the MODX page.
